records.headline: Fog advisory
records.description:
Near-zero visibility in fog is expected.

When:
Now until this afternoon.

Where:
Inland sections of the North Coast.

Remarks:
Areas of dense fog have developed this morning significantly reducing visibilities. The dense fog will dissipate  this afternoon.

Travel will likely be hazardous in some locations. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times.

If driving, turn on your lights, slow down and maintain a safe following distance.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

records.headline: Blowing snow advisory
records.description:
Snow and strong winds will lead to poor visibility in blowing snow in some locations.

Locations: Northern Peninsula East.

Total snowfall: near 5 cm, except 10 to 15 cm south of Hare Bay.

Maximum wind gusts: northeasterly 60 km/h.

Time span: tonight.

Remarks: Conditions are expected to be poorest south of Hare Bay, where the gusty winds will coincide with the most snowfall.

Travel will likely be hazardous in some locations.

Consider postponing non-essential travel and outdoor activities until conditions improve.

Blowing snow advisories are issued when widespread poor visibility in blowing snow is expected.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NLstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NLwx.

records.headline: Snowfall warning
records.description:
Significant snowfall is expected in some areas.

Location: Green Bay - White Bay.

Total snowfall: 5 to 10 cm, except 15 to 20 cm over the Baie Verte Peninsula, as well as Hampden to Jackson's Arm.

Time span: this afternoon until Sunday morning.

Remarks: Precipitation will fall mainly as snow inland and in the vicinity of White Bay, while a mixture of snow and rain will occur elsewhere. The snow is expected to be wet and heavy.

Prepare for quickly changing and deteriorating travel conditions. Allow extra time for travel.

Snowfall warnings are issued when significant impacts are expected due to snowfall accumulations.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NLstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NLwx.

records.area: Coastline of the City of Percé
records.headline: Storm surge warning
records.description:
Higher than normal water levels with large waves are expected near the coast Saturday afternoon.


The combinaison of:
- moderate winds from the northeast
- a weak surge set-up
- a high tidal range
risk of causing a minor wave surge along the coast on Saturday afternoon.

Additional information:
Coastal flooding is likely to occur along the coastline.
Coastal erosion is possible in vulnerable areas.

This warning is issued when high water levels pose a threat to coastal regions due to tides, storm surge and/or waves.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to QCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #QCStorm.

records.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 28 at 12:15PM MST until November 28 at 9:00PM MST by NWS Cheyenne WY
records.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow. Additional snow accumulations up to 4 to 5
inches above 7500 feet. Winds gusting as high as 40 mph.

* WHERE...Sierra Madre Range.

* WHEN...Until 9 PM MST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Outdoor recreation could become dangerous to those caught
unprepared for hazardous winter conditions. Hunters, hikers, and
snowmobilers may become disoriented and lost due to low visibility
in falling and blowing snow. Areas of blowing snow could reduce
visibility and lead to slick road conditions.
records.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
for the state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

records.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 28 at 12:15PM MST until November 28 at 9:00PM MST by NWS Cheyenne WY
records.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow. Additional snow accumulations between 4 and 6
inches. Winds gusting as high as 50 mph.

* WHERE...Snowy Range.

* WHEN...Until 9 PM MST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Outdoor recreation could become life threatening to those
caught unprepared for severe winter conditions. Hikers and
snowmobilers may easily become disoriented. Frostbite and
hypothermia can develop quickly. Widespread blowing snow could
significantly reduce visibility and lead to dangerous travel
conditions.
records.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

records.area: Clear Creek, CO; Grand, CO; Summit, CO
records.headline: Snow Squall Warning issued November 28 at 12:09PM MST until November 28 at 1:15PM MST by NWS Denver CO
records.description:
The National Weather Service in Denver has issued a

* Snow Squall Warning for...
Western Clear Creek County in central Colorado...
Central Summit County in central Colorado...
South Central Grand County in north central Colorado...

* Until 115 PM MST.

* At 1209 PM MST, a dangerous snow squall was located 5 miles west of
Loveland Pass, or 54 miles west of Denver, moving northeast at 50
mph.

HAZARD...Flash freeze on roads and rapidly falling visibility due
to intense bursts of heavy snow and gusty winds. Wind
gusts greater than 50 mph could knock down tree limbs and
blow around unsecured objects.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Dangerous and life-threatening travel conditions are
expected to develop rapidly in the warning area.

* Locations impacted include...
Silverthorne, Frisco, Georgetown, Dillon, Silver Plume, Keystone,
Loveland Pass, Bakerville, Berthoud Falls, Copper Mountain and Vail
Pass.

This includes Interstate 70 between mile markers 190 and 228.
records.instruction:
Slow Down! Rapid changes in visibility and road conditions are
expected with this dangerous snow squall. Be alert for sudden
whiteout conditions.

Wet roadways will quickly freeze. Black ice will cause roads, bridges
and overpasses to become slick and dangerous. Slow down and be
prepared for sudden loss of traction.

records.headline: High Wind Warning issued November 28 at 12:08PM MST until November 28 at 3:00PM MST by NWS Salt Lake City UT
records.description:
* WHAT...Northwest winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 65 mph,
locally up to 75-80 mph.

* WHERE...Castle Country, particularly along SR-10 from Castle Dale
and Orangeville south through Fremont Junction.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM MST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...High winds may move loose debris, damage property and
cause power outages. Strong cross winds can be expected along
Highway 10 where travel could be difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles and vehicles with trailers.
records.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles and vehicles with trailers. Use extra caution.

People are urged to secure loose objects that could be blown around
or damaged by the wind.

records.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 28 at 11:45AM MST by NWS Cheyenne WY
records.description:
At 1143 AM MST...A snow squall was near Arlington, or 32 miles
northwest of Laramie...moving east at 45 mph.

HAZARD...Sudden and brief snowfall rates of 1 to 2 inches per hour,
winds in excess of 35 mph, and visibilities less than one
half mile.

SOURCE...Radar and Webcams.

IMPACT...Hazardous travel conditions slick roads and low
visibilities due to falling and blowing snow.

Locations impacted include...
Laramie, Albany, West Laramie, Antelope Buttes, Nine Mile, Rogers
Canyon, Pelton Creek Campground, Rambler, Vedauwoo Campground, North
Crow Campground, Laramie Regional Airport, The Buttes, Rob Roy
Reservoir, Lake Owen, Hutton Lake, Yellow Pine Campground, Arlington,
Tie City Campground, Harriman Heights, and Vedauwoo.
records.instruction:
Expect rapid changes in weather and road conditions. Motorists are
urged to use extreme caution if traveling through these areas!

Rapid visibility reduction and potentially icy roads are likely to
produce hazardous driving conditions. Travel is not advised during
this snow squall. If you are traveling and encounter adverse winter
driving conditions, reduce speed and make sure headlights are on to
increase the visibility of your vehicle to those around you.

Sharply colder temperatures following the snow will cause any water
or slush to quickly freeze on roads and sidewalks. Untreated road
surfaces will become extremely slippery and offer little or no
traction. Reduced speeds and increased distance between vehicles is
advised.

* WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Surging trade winds will continue to
produce elevated trade-wind swell, leading to elevated surf and

current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

records.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.7 ft of inundation above ground level is

Bays.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.

than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

is expected to be 1.6 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 1:28 PM

Sunday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific
Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
records.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

records.headline: Flood Warning issued November 28 at 8:31AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
records.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Previous rainfall working through the basin will cause river levels
on the St. Johns at Deland to continue rising through Major Flood
Stage. The river is forecast to rise above its former record crest
this weekend, reaching 6.5 feet, then continuing to 6.6 feet early
next week where it is expected to linger into at least mid next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The river is forecast to rise above the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM EST Saturday the stage was 6.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 AM EST Saturday was 6.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise through Major Flood
Stage, reaching 6.5 feet late this weekend, then 6.6 feet early
next week. The river is then forecast to remain steady through at
least mid next week.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
records.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 915 PM EST.

records.headline: Flood Warning issued November 28 at 8:20AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
records.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Rainfall working through the basin has caused river levels on the
St. Johns Above Lake Harney near Geneva to remain within Major Flood
Stage, above its previous record flood stage. River levels are
forecast to begin a very slow decline within Major flood stage this
weekend and through next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The river crest has surpassed its previous flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM EST Saturday the stage was 13.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 AM EST Saturday was 13.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain within Major Flood
Stage. A slow decline from 13.1 feet may begin over the weekend
into early next week.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
records.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 900 PM EST.

records.headline: Flood Warning issued November 28 at 8:17AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
records.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Extreme rainfall across the upper St. Johns River has caused levels
near Cocoa to remain within Major Flood Stage, well above its
previous record flood stage. The river level trends are forecast to
follow a very slow decline through Major Flood Stage through next
week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The crest has exceeded the previous flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 AM EST Saturday the stage was 18.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:15 AM EST Saturday was 18.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is forecast to show a very slow decline from
18.2 feet to 17.7 feet from this weekend and through next week.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

records.description:

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Past heavy rainfall working its way through the basin will cause
levels on the St Johns River at Astor to remain steady within Major
Flood Stage between 4.3 and 4.4 feet well into next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth

Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are
inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive
and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Camptround are

records.headline: Flood Warning issued November 28 at 5:50AM EST until November 30 at 3:00AM EST by NWS Boston/Norton MA
records.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Massachusetts...

Taunton River Near Bridgewater affecting Bristol and Plymouth
Counties.

For the Taunton River...including Bridgewater...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Taunton River near Bridgewater.

* WHEN...Until late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Backwater flooding from the Taunton River
will cause flooding of lower Purchade Brook in Middleboro.  This
will cause Woloski Park to become impassable by most vehicles.
Beware of the dangers of crossing flooded roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:45 AM EST Saturday the stage was 8.3 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 4:45 AM EST Saturday was 8.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 8.4 feet
this afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage late tomorrow
evening.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
records.instruction:
Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 600 PM EST.

records.headline: Dense Fog Advisory issued November 27 at 4:06PM PST until November 28 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Hanford CA
records.description:
* WHAT...Visibility one quarter mile or less in dense fog. Some
locations will experience zero visibility for several hours. This
dense fog event will be a Level 4 on a scale of 1 to 5.

* WHERE...Much of central California.

* WHEN...From 8 PM this evening to Noon PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Dense fog will make driving conditions hazardous leading
to a high transportation risk.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Dense fog will resemble that of the past two
days. Low clouds will quickly become dense fog shortly after
sunset. Be aware that dense fog will be widespread by late this
evening, if you are traveling.
records.instruction:
If driving, slow down, use your low beam headlights, and leave plenty
of distance ahead of you. Consider leaving after the dense fog has
gone. Be sure to change your headlights from AUTO to MANUAL, since
automatic headlights will not activate in the dense fog.

records.headline: Flood Warning issued November 25 at 2:07PM MST until November 30 at 3:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
records.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by an upstream dam release is expected.

* WHERE...Central Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 300 PM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 202 PM MST, a streamflow gauge near Dateland continues to
steadily rise and is now showing a depth of just above 7.5 feet
with flow around 1250 cfs. This gauge is forecasted to reach
action stage (8 ft) on Friday. Flooding is expected along the
Gila River within the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
records.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

records.area: North Sea coast at Bridlington - Harbour Road and Floral Pavilion
records.event: Flood Warning: North Sea coast at Bridlington - Harbour Road and Floral Pavilion
records.headline: Flooding is expected: North Sea coast at Bridlington - Harbour Road and Floral Pavilion
records.description:
High tides and forecast weather conditions are expected to cause flooding this evening. 

Flooding is expected from 18:15 to 21:45 on 28/11/2026. 

High astronomical tides and a large surge is expected.
Locations most affected will be coastal roads, promenades and footpaths.. 

We are closely monitoring the situation . 

Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded. Stay away from promenades where overtopping is possible. 

This message will be updated by 2:00AM on Sunday 29 November or as the situation changes.
records.instruction:
Act now 
 
You should: 
- go to Check for flooding for a map of the area and to monitor up-to-date local flood information – https://check-for-flooding.service.gov.uk/target-area/122FWC001  
- act on your personal flood plan if you have one - https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/personal-flood-plan 
- follow the guidance in 'What to do before or during a flood' - https://www.gov.uk/help-during-flood  
 
You can also read more about what flood warnings are – https://www.gov.uk/guidance/flood-alerts-and-warnings-what-they-are-and-what-to-do#flood-warning 
 
Stay up to date 
 
To get the latest flood information, you can: 
- go to Check for flooding 
- monitor local weather, news and travel updates 
- call Floodline on 0345 988 1188, using quickdial code 130501
records.sourceName: UK Met Office via Meteoalarm / EUMETNET

records.headline: Moderate Cold Stress
records.description:
Strong cold stress expected.

Risk of frostbite and hypothermia. Difficulties with outdoor work. Increased load on social services (especially care for the homeless) and the healthcare system.
records.instruction: Wear appropriate clothing, limit outdoor activities, especially during the coldest part of the day (usually morning). Schedule higher physical activity for the warmer part of the day. Monitor your health. Plan your travel with regard to the current traffic situation.
records.sourceName: Czech Hydrometeorological Institute (ČHMÚ) via Meteoalarm / EUMETNET

records.headline: Moderate Cold Related Impact
records.description:
Minimum air temperatures below -12 °C.

Possible complications, especially in rail transport. Freezing of turnouts (points) in rail transport. Possible water mains failures.
records.instruction: Check the functionality of all heating systems and backup power systems. Plan trips carefully and monitor the traffic situation. For electric vehicles, monitor the battery charge status and recharge in time.
records.sourceName: Czech Hydrometeorological Institute (ČHMÚ) via Meteoalarm / EUMETNET

records.area: Moravskoslezský kraj (Bílovec, Bruntál, Český Těšín, Frýdek-Místek, Havířov, Kopřivnice, Nový Jičín, Odry, Ostrava, Rýmařov, Vítkov)
records.headline: Moderate Snow Related Impact
records.description:
A combination of snow and stronger winds will cause up to 400 formation of snow drifts.

Complications in road transport. Travel disruptions due to route closures, vehicle collisions (accumulated snow, reduced visibility).
records.instruction: Drive and walk carefully. Stay informed of the driving conditions. Mandatory equipment: winter tires with sufficient tread depth, snow chains in mountain areas. In the mountains, follow instructions of the Mountain Rescue Service.
